html:
Hong Kong cinema, the films made in the colony, became one of the world's great film industries from the 1970s to the 1990s, famous for martial arts and action.

The Shaw Brothers studio made Mandarin martial arts films from the 1960s. In 1970 Golden Harvest was founded and signed Bruce Lee, whose films made kung fu known around the world. Jackie Chan mixed fighting with comedy and stunts; John Woo made gunfights operatic; Wong Kar-wai brought a dreamy art cinema.

At its peak Hong Kong was one of the largest film exporters in the world, selling its films, mostly in Cantonese, across Asia. Its style shaped Hollywood action films. After the handover, piracy, mainland co-productions and censorship shrank it, though it remains a centre of Chinese language film, alongside the films of Taiwan and the mainland.
sum: Hong Kong cinema, the films made in the colony, became one of the world's great film industries from the 1970s to the 1990s, famous for martial arts and action.
